scenarios.description: Full nesting stack traversal: sequence 8 successive interrupts with strictly increasing priorities (7 down to 0), pulsing `cpu_ack` for each, verifying `nest_level` reaches 8, followed by 8 successive `cpu_eoi` pulses returning `nest_level` to 0.
Equal priority tie-breaking: configure channels 2, 4, and 7 to priority level 2, assert all three simultaneously, and verify that acknowledge dispatches IRQ2 first, IRQ4 second, and IRQ7 third.

Edge vs Level trigger qualification: configure IRQ0 as edge-triggered and IRQ1 as level-triggered; pulse IRQ0 and hold IRQ1 high across CPU ACK and EOI cycles, verifying IRQ0 clears on ACK while IRQ1 remains pending until deasserted externally.

Masking and dynamic priority demotion while IRQ asserted: assert IRQ3 with priority 2 to raise `cpu_irq`, then write MASK[3]=1 or change PRIO_2_3 to priority 6 while an active nesting priority 4 is running, verifying immediate deassertion of `cpu_irq`.

requirements.description: Priority values range from 0 (highest urgency) to 7 (lowest urgency); if two enabled pending interrupts share identical priority values, the lower channel ID (e.g. IRQ0 over IRQ1) takes precedence.

An interrupt request is only dispatched (`cpu_irq` asserted) if its priority is strictly higher (numerically lower) than the current priority level on top of the nesting stack (or if nest_level == 0).

Pulsing `cpu_ack` for 1 clock cycle while `cpu_irq` is asserted clears the corresponding PEND bit for edge-triggered channels (or keeps it cleared until next edge), pushes the servicing interrupt's priority onto the nesting stack, increments `nest_level`, and deasserts `cpu_irq` if no higher-priority interrupt is pending.
For level-triggered channels, PEND remains asserted as long as the external `irq_src` bit remains high, but re-arbitration only occurs if its priority exceeds the current nesting threshold.
Pulsing `cpu_eoi` for 1 clock cycle pops the nesting stack, decrements `nest_level`, and restores the previous active execution priority threshold.
Register writes take effect immediately on the next rising clock edge and trigger re-evaluation of arbitration and `cpu_irq` state.
When `nest_level` equals 8, no further interrupts may preempt; `cpu_irq` remains deasserted until at least one `cpu_eoi` is received.
`cpu_ack` must only be asserted when `cpu_irq` is 1; asserting `cpu_ack` when `cpu_irq` is 0 is ignored without modifying nesting stack.
`cpu_eoi` should only be asserted when `nest_level` > 0; asserting `cpu_eoi` when `nest_level` == 0 has no effect on stack or level.
Register writes to address space 0x0 to 0x9 occur on clock cycles where `reg_we` is 1; read data `reg_rdata` is output combinational or 1-cycle registered matching register address `reg_addr`.
Simultaneous assertion of `cpu_ack` and `cpu_eoi` on the same cycle: the `cpu_eoi` pops first followed by `cpu_ack` push (effective replace of top of stack), net `nest_level` change is 0.
`cpu_vector` updates in the same cycle `cpu_irq` asserts and remains stable as long as `cpu_irq` remains asserted unless a higher priority interrupt preempts it before acknowledge.

goals.rationale: Overall functional coverage across all interrupt modes, arbitration states, and stack depths.
Cross of channel ID (0-7) x priority level (0-7) x trigger mode (edge vs level) during successful dispatch.
Cross of nest_level (0 to 8) x CPU handshake events (cpu_ack, cpu_eoi, simultaneous ack+eoi).
